BT6: https://bt6.gg Dreadnode:   / dreadnode   Zenity:   / zenitysec   0DIN, Mozilla's AI bug bounty: https://0din.ai -------- For 25 years, cross-site scripting was how you stole a victim's data. AI assistants brought it back as a whole new bug class. #HackingLikeIts1999 Ads Dawson (Staff AI Security Researcher at Dreadnode, #2 in the USA on HackerOne) and Mike Takahashi (AI Red Team Researcher at Zenity, 400+ vulnerabilities reported) are both members of BT6. They spent the past year getting AI assistants in production to leak user data, and in this talk they walk through six of those attack chains, all reported and fixed. They show how they got around the usual defenses, then share the repeatable method they use to find these bugs, so you can start hunting for them yourself. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Chapters 0:00 Intro 0:22 whoami 1:15 AI Exfil and XSS are the same primitive 2:58 agenda 3:23 Bug #1: Meta AI Universal Chat CAPTCHA Data Exfil (one Unicode char away from a bounty) 6:14 Bug #2: Business Assistant Backdoor (the 2-for-1 bug) 6:27 Stage 1: 8:26 Tip: Prompt Stuffing 8:57 Stage 2: Make it persistent 10:45 Bug #3: Steal Private Facebook Posts in Contemplation Mode 12:27 Tip: Denial-of-X Attacks with AI 12:55 Bug #4: WhatsApp mailto: Encryption bypass with Persistent Context 15:23 Bug #5: Meta AI Invisible Prompt + Allowlist Bypass 15:54 Technique 1: Invisible Unicode in Prompt Autofill Param 16:34 Technique 2: Domain Allowlist Bypass w/ Image Proxy 17:38 Bug #6: Tiramisu Technique (prompt injection via MCP tool description) 20:27 The Repeatable Method (how to start hunting for these yourself) 21:44 This slide makes you rich 23:24 Q&A 23:35 Q: What would you say to hunters getting their prompt injection bugs marked as dupes...because prompt injection. ----------------------------------------------------------------------
